Read "a = 1" in m as declaring a local a of m. y refers to the global a (= 3).
- m: local a = 1, then a = y [latex]-[/latex] a = 3 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 2.
- n(a): x refers to m's local a. With dynamic scoping, the a inside n is also m's a (the most recent active a). x = x [latex]\times[/latex] a = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 4, and since x is that same a, a becomes 4. Prints 4.
- Back in m: print(a) prints 4.

Answer: 4,4

questions.text: An operator delete(i) for a binary heap data structure is to be designed to delete the item in the i-th node.Assume that the heap is implemented in an array and i refers to the i-th index of thearray.If the heap tree has depth d (number of edges on the path from the root to the farthest leaf),the n what is the time complexity to re-fix the heap efficiently after the removal of the element?
questions.solution:
To delete node i: move the last element into position i, then either sift it up or down. Either way it moves along one root-to-leaf path, at most d levels [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(d)[/latex]. It can take that long, so it is not [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: O(d) but not O(1)

questions.text:
Consider the weighted undirected graph with 4 vertices,where the weigh to edge {i, j} is given by the entry Wij in the matrix W.
[latex]W=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2&8 & 5\\ 2& 0& 5 &8 \\ 8 & 5 & 0& x\\ 5&8 & x&0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
The largest possible integer value of x, for which at least one shortest path between some pair of vertices will contain the edge with weight x is ____.
questions.solution:
Without edge {3, 4}, the shortest path from 3 to 4 is 3-2-1-4 = 5 + 2 + 5 = 12.

The edge of weight x lies on a shortest path (at least one, possibly tied) only if [latex]x\le12[/latex]. The largest integer is 12.

Answer: 12

questions.text: Let G be a complete undirected graph on 4 vertices, having 6 edges  with weights being 1,2,3,4,5, and 6. The maximum possible weight that a minimum weight spanning tree of G can haveis .
questions.solution:
An MST of 4 vertices has 3 edges; edges 1 and 2 are always taken (two edges cannot form a cycle).

To make the third edge as heavy as possible, put edges 1, 2, 3 in a triangle, so 3 is rejected. The 4th vertex must then be joined by the next lightest edge, 4.

Maximum MST weight = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7

Answer: 7

questions.text:
G = (V,E) is an undirected simple graph in which each edge has a distinct weight,and e is a particular edgeof G. Which of the following statements about the minimum spanning trees (MSTs) of G is/are TRUE?
I. If e is the lightest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G includes e
II. If e is the heaviest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G excludes e
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: the lightest edge of one cycle can still be the heaviest edge of another cycle and be excluded [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: cycle property: with distinct weights, the heaviest edge of any cycle is in no MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: II only
